chapter: Chick Webb, Lucky Roberts, Alex Jackson
title: Alex Jackson's band: Detroit and the road west
summary: Charlie Johnson recommends Scott to Jackson; they open in Detroit in 1932 then head to California.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Now, see, from then on I'm not working a long time with anybody because things were beginning to change then. And I wanted to travel. I wanted to see some of the United States. I hadn't seen it. I'd been to just Washington, D.C., around the horn, that's Philadelphia, Baltimore and Washington, with the show. And I hadn't seen anything out West.

Well, I played some gigs with Lucky Roberts, yeah. Nice, nice, very nice. And then the same Talley Johnson called me one night and says, Scottie, when you get off there, stop by, I want to tell you something. Well, after I got through

work, I went by and he told me, there's a new band in town, Alex Jackson, from Cincinnati, Ohio. And he said, I had a commitment to play in Detroit, but I'm anchored here with Ed Small and I have a contract I have to-- and I know this guy, Jackson, he's a nice fellow.

And you said you'd never been out West. Here's a good chance for you to do it. I'll tell him about you. Alex Jackson. Well, he was a nice handsome man. I said, well, why not, to myself. And Charlie said, well, Scottie, here's your chance.

Well, he formed the band. We opened up in Detroit. Now, this is '32. Opened up in Detroit. Grand Boulevard and Joy Road, the Mirror Ballroom. And we stayed there six months. And I lived in Detroit, and I found -- that's Motor City, and (unintelligible) for almost nothing. $100, and I got a car. Well, it was a used car, but just to get around.

That was nice, very nice. We came back, then we came to this home town. Then he wanted to go out West. He had been booked. So we went to Chicago, Cleveland, Chicago and all that, and then finally, California. And we were booked ahead. Well, I don't got a whole lot of experience -- at the same time, I was sending money back home. And my mother, she was saving it for me. Can you beat that?
What a woman. And that's how -- I wanted to see the Golden Gate of San Francisco.
